name: noctalia-ipc
description: The shell IPC verbs this project sends, with the arguments each one takes and the line of the pinned release each was read from. data/design/noctalia.json records the configuration keys the shell has; this record is the other half of the same surface -- the commands that read and write them while the session is running -- and the settings application, the session's own keybinds and the scripts under scripts/ may not send a verb that is not listed here.
_note: Kept apart from noctalia.json because the two answer different questions and are verified differently: a config key is a field in a schema struct, a verb is an entry in the command table, and a key can exist with no verb that reaches it (Do Not Disturb is exactly that case -- IPC only, no key at all in v5.4.1). One trap this record exists to prevent: the command table's header also declares positional-argument names and choice values as string literals, so extracting every quoted string from src/cli/schema_msg.h yields 204 names of which only some are commands. `monitor-selector` is the clearest example -- it is a positional several bar commands accept, not a verb, and sending it would be refused at runtime rather than caught here. Every entry below was matched against an `inline constexpr Command` definition. The table declares 119 of them at this ref, so what follows is a curated subset and not a census, and the distinction has already cost something: a cell of the A to Z table in data/design/keybinds.json was reserved for a wallpaper step on the grounds that noctalia v5.4.1 had no wallpaper verb, when `wallpaper-next` was at :842 all along with an optional connector and two siblings beside it. A verb missing from this file is a gap in this file until the header says otherwise.

verified_against.reply_note: The handler prints one line and exits non-zero when it refuses. iarch/lib/modes.py reads the reply text rather than trusting the exit code, because a handler that answers 'ok' as a no-op -- caffeine already in that state, src/idle/idle_inhibitor.cpp:175-212 -- and a handler that could not be reached are different facts and only the text tells them apart.

source: noctalia-dev/noctalia at v5.4.1: src/cli/schema_msg.h (the Command table, its Positional declarations and its choice lists), src/app/application_ipc.cpp:158-159 (what a handler prints for Do Not Disturb) and src/idle/idle_inhibitor.cpp:175-212 (what caffeine answers, including the no-op ok), src/launcher/panel_catalog.cpp:25-35 (the nine builtin panel ids a panel verb may name) and src/launcher/dmenu_cli.h (the `noctalia dmenu` stdin/stdout picker, which is a subcommand of the binary and not a `msg` verb, so it is not listed below; scripts/iarch-run.sh is what sends it and docs/UNVERIFIED.md KB-10 carries its unobserved behaviour)

arguments.name: action
arguments.note: This project sends 'lock', 'suspend' and 'lock-and-suspend' only. not_used.why: This application offers Lock now and Suspend and stops there. A control panel that can end a session, reboot or power off the machine turns one mis-click into lost work, and the shell's own session menu already draws those actions with the confirmation the shell owns.
not_used.evidence: src/cli/schema_msg.h:79-80 lists the seven actions; SECURITY.md's rule that a diagnostic or a panel never takes an action it was not asked for

not_used.why: Syncing the login screen needs the polkit action org.noctalia.greeter.sync-appearance and a state directory owned by root, which is why Part 3 recorded the whole greeter surface and emitted nothing. A settings row that prompts for administrative authentication to change a screen the user is not looking at is not a feature this project ships.
not_used.evidence: src/cli/schema_msg.h:530 and data/design/greeter.json (auto_sync and privilege_command are withheld)

not_used.why: Despite the name, this is an audio effects profile (its kind choices are output and input), not a glass effect profile. Recorded because the name invites exactly the wrong mapping from this project's own `preset` and `effects` switches.
